verdicts.question: What does Scrapr (The Kabadiwala) charge partner kabadiwalas (subscription or commission), and how many of its kabadiwalas are active in Bengaluru? Is ScrapUncle actually operating in Bengaluru or only Delhi NCR?
verdicts.problems: Verification was impossible on this machine: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200 of 200) before the sceptic pass began, and direct fetches (curl) are denied, so not one cited source could be checked against a snippet. Judged on what the repository itself holds: (1) The central claim, Scrapr's lead-subscription tiers (15 free leads; Starter Rs 49/5 leads; Pro Rs 199/35 leads; Unlimited Rs 499 with the 50-lead / Rs 20,000 / 6-hours-online refund condition; Rs 299 kit with 10 free leads), rests solely on the researcher's own 'read 29 Sep 2026' of scrapr.app/scrapr-partner/pricing. The independent 29 Sep research pass (docs/plan/research/competitors-b2c.md, open question 1) recorded that Scrapr's pricing page returned 404 that same day. Either a different URL path worked later or the figures are unconfirmed; nothing in the repo corroborates any of the rupee amounts, the lead counts or the refund condition. Not confirmed by snippet. (2) TKW Partner app id app.scrapr.partner, '10K+ installs, updated 18 Aug 2026', and the ScrapUncle Play wording 'currently available in most parts of Delhi NCR' (updated 19 Sep 2026): not confirmed; the earlier pass states Play Store pages could not be read. (3) Deccan Herald 5 Aug 2026 article and its '10 kg minimum' for ScrapUncle: not confirmed anywhere else in the repo; note the earlier pass attributes a '10 kg free-pickup promise' to The Kabadiwala app reviews, not ScrapUncle, so the 10 kg figure may have been transposed. (4) Scrapr terms 'dated 20 May 2024' and the 'collection charges / surge' wording: not confirmed. (5) Minor discrepancy: the answer says the Bangalore page lists 24 localities; the earlier pass read the same page as '25+ Bengaluru neighbourhoods'. (6) The '30-100 active partner kabadiwalas in Bengaluru' default is an inference from an unconfirmed national install count and is not sourced; the answer does label it a default, which is acceptable, but the arithmetic behind 'dozens to low hundreds' is not shown. What IS corroborated by the independent 29 Sep pass: Scrapr is The Kabadiwala's partner marketplace run by ASAR Green Kabadi Pvt Ltd, claims 5,000+ kabadiwalas, 11 cities (Scrapr) / 15 cities (Sankalp Forum, 23 Sep 2025), household chooses a partner by distance and price; ScrapUncle's rate page lists Bengaluru alongside Delhi NCR; Inc42 28 Jan 2026 Rs 22 Cr pre-Series A, 300K+ pickups, 20M kg, Delhi NCR focus. Refined-model gap: the answer never says which of the founder's five price levels these competitors touch (both are L1 household-to-collector players; ScrapUncle, running its own crews and collection centres and planning an e-waste plant, also internalises L2 and acts as its own yard and e-waste dismantler/pre-processor), nor that Scrapr's partner model leaves the L2 kabadiwala-to-yard hand-off unrecorded, which is exactly where Luma.Green's S1-S3 state tracking and lot records differentiate.
verdicts.correction: What is established (corroborated by the separate 29 Sep research pass in docs/plan/research/competitors-b2c.md and its sources): Scrapr is The Kabadiwala's partner-kabadiwala marketplace, run by ASAR Green Kabadi Pvt Ltd; in metros including Bengaluru it routes household bookings to local partner kabadiwalas, the household choosing by distance and price (Sankalp Forum interview with co-founder Anurag Asati, 23 Sep 2025; scrapr.app/city/bangalore). Scrapr claims 5,000+ kabadiwalas and 11 cities on its site (15 cities per Sankalp) and about 25 Bengaluru neighbourhoods (Koramangala, Indiranagar, Jayanagar and others) with no partner names or counts. ScrapUncle (Swapeco Solutions, Delhi) raised Rs 22 Cr pre-Series A on 28 Jan 2026 to expand across Delhi NCR (Inc42; 300K+ pickups, 20M kg) and its public rate page lists a Bengaluru rate card next to Delhi NCR. What is NOT confirmed and must be treated as an open item until someone opens the pages or installs the apps: (a) the partner fee model and every figure in it (the Rs 49/199/499 lead plans, 15 free leads, Rs 299 kit, refund condition); the same-day independent pass found the pricing page returning 404, so record it as 'reported once, unverified'; (b) the TKW Partner app's 10K+ installs; (c) ScrapUncle's Play wording restricting service to Delhi NCR, and the Deccan Herald 5 Aug 2026 mention with a 10 kg minimum (the 10 kg figure appears in the earlier pass as a The Kabadiwala app-review complaint, so it may belong to the wrong company); (d) the Bengaluru partner headcount, for which no public figure exists; a working default of 'tens to low hundreds' is a guess, not data. Actions that settle this in a day: open scrapr.app/scrapr-partner/pricing and screenshot it; install 'TKW Partner - Buy Kabad' on a Bengaluru phone and read the paywall; book one ScrapUncle pickup in a pilot ward and one The Kabadiwala pickup in each of 5 Bengaluru areas and count distinct partners; email contact@scrapr.app. Against the refined chain: both competitors sit at price level L1 (collector to household); ScrapUncle also internalises L2 (it is its own yard) and, with a planned e-waste plant, the dismantler/pre-processor role; Scrapr leaves the L2 kabadiwala-to-yard hand-off and material states S1-S3 unrecorded, which is Luma.Green's opening. Decision to keep regardless of the unconfirmed figures: kabadiwala tools free for the pilot; position against ScrapUncle on Kannada, no weight minimum, and household choice of buyer; status should be 'needs-pilot-or-counsel' rather than 'partly' until the pricing page is seen.

verdicts.question: What do Recykal.Market and Attero's MetalMandi charge small aggregators, and what minimum lot sizes and payment terms do they set? Do the Android apps of The Kabadiwala, ScrapUncle, MetalMandi and Recykal offer Indian languages?
verdicts.problems: No source could be checked by snippet: the WebSearch budget was exhausted before this pass and page fetches are blocked, so every verdict below rests on cross-checking against the separate 29 Sep research pass held in the repository. Corroborated there: Recykal.Market's home-page claims (10K+ verified GST-registered businesses, 3M+ tonnes, Rs 2,500 Cr+, 28+ states), that Recykal deals only with GST-verified sellers, the Forbes India 2 Sep 2021 article ('marketplace fee', rate undisclosed), the Tribune 7 Apr 2026 MetalMandi figures (2 lakh+ downloads, 1.1 lakh registered, 50,000+ MAU, about 15,000 t/month, 100+ cities), MetalMandi's launch in early 2025, '675 recyclers' for Recykal, and that the iOS listings of The Kabadiwala, ScrapUncle and Recykal Seller show English only. NOT confirmed by any snippet or earlier pass: (1) every quoted clause from Recykal's Terms of Use ('Recykal shall raise invoices towards the platform fees', negotiable MOQs, '7, 15, 30 days' credit, buyer must fund escrow before dispatch, debit-note QC deductions, rejected truck returns at seller's cost); the earlier B2B brief read Recykal as 'moderated deals; no escrow stated', which conflicts with the escrow-before-dispatch claim, so this needs a first-hand read. (2) MetalMandi FAQ 'zero commission' dated 26 Mar 2026, the Financial Express and CNBC-TV18 articles of 13 Apr 2026 (Attero sole buyer; opening to third-party buyers; 'a certain percentage of the traded value'), and the NEFT/RTGS-after-inspection payment wording. The Economic Times 15 Jan 2025 launch story with 'zero transaction fees' is plausible and consistent with the earlier pass's launch date but not itself confirmed. (3) All four Google Play descriptions being English-only and their 'updated' dates (18 Sep, 19 Sep, 11 Sep, 15 Sep 2026), the Recykal Seller package id com.rapidue.uzed with 100K+ downloads, and MetalMandi's 500K+ Play downloads: the earlier pass states Play Store pages could not be read on 29 Sep. (4) Internal inconsistency left unreconciled: MetalMandi '500K+' Play downloads (11 Sep 2026) versus '2 lakh+ downloads' (Tribune, 7 Apr 2026), and '500+ cities' on the home page versus '100+ cities' in the Tribune; plausible growth, but the answer should say which figure it relies on. (5) Omitted fact from the earlier pass that matters for Bengaluru: MetalMandi's main hubs are Delhi NCR, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad, and Bengaluru is not among them. No arithmetic errors found. Refined-model gaps: the answer does not place either platform on the founder's L1-L5 price levels or S0-S9 states. Recykal.Market trades bales (S3), flakes (S4-S6) and granules (S7) at L3 and L4; MetalMandi is a recycler-owned buying app, so its 'price' is Attero's L3 bid (for e-waste, the dismantler/pre-processor level), not a neutral market price. The decision's 'soft 100 kg floor, no hard minimum below yard level' mixes levels: 100 kg is an L2 (kabadiwala-to-yard) figure, while L3 lots of bales or flakes move by truckload (Recykal's 'before the truck returns' language), so minimums should be set per material state, not one platform-wide number. The by-product listings (bagasse, fly ash, slag etc.) the founder added are outside both competitors' catalogues, which is worth saying as a positioning point.
verdicts.correction: What can be stated with corroboration from the separate 29 Sep pass: Recykal.Market (Rapidue Technologies) publishes no fee schedule; Forbes India (2 Sep 2021) says only that it 'makes a marketplace fee', so the percentage is an open item. It deals only with GST-verified sellers (KYC with GST certificate, PAN and bank details), which excludes unregistered kabadiwalas; it claims 10,000+ verified businesses, 3 Mn+ tonnes and Rs 2,500 Cr+ traded across 28+ states, and about 675 recyclers. Attero's MetalMandi launched in January 2025 as a recycler-owned buying app; by 7 Apr 2026 (Tribune) it had 2 lakh+ downloads, 1.1 lakh registered users, about 50,000 monthly actives and about 15,000 t/month across 100+ cities, with main hubs in Delhi NCR, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad and Bengaluru not among them. The iOS listings of The Kabadiwala, ScrapUncle and Recykal Seller declare English as their only language. Unconfirmed, keep as open items with a named check: (a) Recykal's terms on invoiced platform fees, negotiable MOQs, 7/15/30-day credit, escrow-before-dispatch and debit-note deductions (one earlier read saw no escrow stated; open recykal.market/terms-and-conditions and quote it, then ask Recykal sales +91 77999 96255 for the fee percentage); (b) MetalMandi's 'zero commission' FAQ, NEFT/RTGS-after-inspection terms, and the April 2026 plan to charge a percentage once third-party buyers join (open metalmandi.in/faqs and the FE/CNBC-TV18 pieces of 13 Apr 2026); (c) whether any of the four Android apps has an in-app Indian-language switch: Play descriptions were not readable on 29 Sep by the earlier pass, so the only reliable test is a 15-minute install on a Kannada- and Hindi-locale phone; (d) reconcile MetalMandi's 500K+ Play badge and '500+ cities' with the Tribune's 2 lakh+ and 100+ cities by citing one dated figure. Against the refined chain: Recykal.Market trades at L3 and L4 in states S3 (bales), S4-S6 (flakes, washed, dried) and S7 (granules); MetalMandi's price is Attero's own L3 bid for metal and e-waste (dismantler/pre-processor level), not a neutral market rate; neither lists industrial by-products such as bagasse, fly ash, slag or foundry sand. Decision, restated by level: zero platform fee for pilot business trades; minimum lot per material state rather than one floor (soft 100 kg at L2 for sorted S2 material; truckload-scale MOQs for S3 bales and S4-S7 feedstock at L3/L4, to be set with the first pre-processor partner); simulated escrow funded before dispatch with settlement options and a QC deduction flow, while marking the 7/15/30-day benchmark as 'reported, unverified'; ship Kannada, Hindi and English UI at launch, since no competitor's store listing advertises an Indian language. Status should be 'needs-pilot-or-counsel' rather than 'partly' until the terms pages are quoted first-hand.
